summary: The document attempts to outline a Food Delivery Mobile App but consists of only seven vague high‑level statements. It lacks any concrete functional breakdown, non‑functional requirements, user roles, security considerations, acceptance criteria, or testability guidance. Consequently, the architectural intent, system boundaries, and stakeholder expectations are undefined.

risk_factors.title: Absence of Security Requirements
risk_factors.description: The document explicitly states "No security requirements" and provides no guidance for authentication, authorization, data encryption, or protection of payment information.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define a security requirements section covering OWASP Top 10 controls, PCI‑DSS compliance for payment data, secure storage of credentials, and transport layer encryption (TLS 1.3).

risk_factors.title: Unspecified Payment Handling
risk_factors.description: Requirement 4 "Customers can pay somehow" gives no detail on payment flow, data collection, or compliance with GDPR/PCI‑DSS.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify payment gateway integration, tokenization of card data, consent handling, and data retention policies. Include privacy impact assessment.

risk_factors.title: Performance Uncertainty
risk_factors.description: Requirement 3 "Delivery should happen fast" lacks measurable latency targets for order processing, dispatch, or UI responsiveness.
risk_factors.mitigation: Add quantitative performance NFRs (e.g., order confirmation < 2 seconds, UI render < 100 ms, delivery ETA accuracy ±5 min).

risk_factors.title: Operational Monitoring Gap
risk_factors.description: No mention of logging, health monitoring, or alerting for the mobile app or backend services.
risk_factors.mitigation: Introduce operational requirements for centralized logging, metrics collection (Prometheus), and alerting (PagerDuty) with defined SLAs.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Replace with measurable quality attributes such as "The app shall achieve a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of ≥ 50 and a crash rate < 0.5% per session."
Define usability metrics, e.g., "A new user can place an order within three taps and ≤ 60 seconds on first use."
Specify supported payment methods (credit card, Apple Pay, Google Pay) and required flow steps.
Detail notification types, delivery channels, and timing, e.g., "Push notification sent within 5 seconds of order status change."

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Without a defined scope, stakeholders cannot agree on boundaries, leading to scope creep and misaligned expectations.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Add a concise scope statement, business goals, and success criteria (e.g., target market, launch date, revenue targets).

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Roles such as Customer, Restaurant Owner, Delivery Driver, and Admin are not identified, preventing proper access control design.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define each role, associated permissions, and persona descriptions.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Only high‑level bullet points exist; detailed use cases, data inputs/outputs, and error handling are absent, making implementation ambiguous.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Provide numbered functional requirements (e.g., REQ‑01: Browse restaurant catalog, REQ‑02: Add items to cart, etc.) with acceptance criteria.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: System capacity, response time, and uptime expectations are not captured, risking under‑provisioned infrastructure.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Add measurable NFRs: peak concurrent users, API latency, 99.9% availability, auto‑scaling rules.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No security controls, data protection, or regulatory compliance (PCI‑DSS, GDPR) are addressed, exposing the project to legal and breach risks.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Include authentication (OAuth 2.0), authorization (RBAC), encryption standards, secure coding guidelines, and compliance checklists.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Without clear criteria, verification cannot be performed, leading to subjective sign‑off.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define pass/fail criteria for each requirement and map to automated test cases.

missing_sections_and_details.section_name: Architecture Overview and System Context Diagram
missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No high‑level architecture, component diagram, or integration points are described, hindering design and impact analysis.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Provide a diagram showing mobile client, API gateway, order service, payment service, notification service, and data stores.

missing_sections_and_details.section_name: Data Model and Privacy Impact Assessment
missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Data entities (User, Order, Payment) and privacy considerations are missing, making data governance impossible.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Include ER diagram, data classification, retention policy, and DPA outcomes.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No guidance on logging, monitoring, incident response, or release management.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specify logging standards, monitoring dashboards, SLA targets, and CI/CD pipeline requirements.

rtm_matrix.test_case_verification: Automated UI test: order placed within 3 taps and ≤ 60 seconds
End‑to‑end latency from order acceptance to driver assignment < 30 seconds
PCI‑DSS compliant tokenization flow validated by security test suite
CRUD operations on menu items verified by integration tests
Notification delivered within 5 seconds of status change (automated push test)
Report generation time < 10 seconds for 1 M records

ai_recommendations: Rewrite all requirements using the SMART format (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time‑bound) and assign unique IDs.
Add a dedicated Security Requirements section that references OWASP Top 10, PCI‑DSS, and GDPR/HIPAA where applicable, with concrete controls.
Create a traceability matrix linking each functional and non‑functional requirement to design components, test cases, and compliance checks to ensure full coverage.
